$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-08-28 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report 5dcab477. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v19 indexes (sub2api INDEX 0a6bfbe2, attestor INDEX c384468f) built by publish-tee-images run 33155344730; the keyless signatures verify against certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market, and the Fulcio certificates embed githubWorkflowSha = the sourceCommit below. This release adds usage-pattern abuse detection with optional automatic rate-limiting, SHIPPED DISABLED (enabled=false, auto_throttle=false) so operators can review the thresholds against their own traffic before turning it on. The detector deliberately does NOT ban accounts or forfeit balances: it can only observe traffic shape, and legitimate batch work (labelling, evals, content processing) is indistinguishable from bulk extraction at that layer. Throttling is reversible; a ban is not, and we could not evidence one. Thresholds were derived from measured production traffic: a heavy Claude Code session shows ~0.999 cache-hit ratio and ~2 real input tokens per request, so the 0.30 / 200 gates sit far from normal use. Earlier releases in this line: proof-v18 (take-offline copy), proof-v17 (reference-source fix + first-screen 1332KB->118KB), proof-v16/v15 (two-sided marketplace). osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation.
